sub_skills.name: Add, subtract, and combine like terms
sub_skills.definition: Simplify a sum or difference of terms or of polynomials by grouping like terms, including subtracting a parenthesized polynomial.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The given expression (after any stated substitution) contains NO product in which a factor is a sum (other than a leading +/- sign before parentheses), no radical/rational/negative exponent and no variable denominator; the work is grouping like terms.

sub_skills.name: Expand and multiply
sub_skills.definition: Multiply out products (constant or monomial x sum, binomial x polynomial, squared binomial, product of monomials) into a sum of terms.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The given expression contains a product with a sum as a factor, or a product of monomials, AND the target form (choices or the stated form) is expanded (a sum of terms). If the target is a product, use EE.3 instead.

sub_skills.name: Factor polynomials (and rewrite quadratic forms)
sub_skills.definition: Rewrite an expanded polynomial as a product (GCF, trinomial, grouping, difference of squares, perfect square) or in completed-square form; identify a factor.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The target form is a product or vertex form ((...)(...), k(...), (x+h)^2+k), or the stem asks which expression is / has a factor. Tag even when CB solves it by expanding the target form and matching coefficients. In an EE.4/EE.5 question, co-tag EE.3 only when a trinomial, difference of squares or perfect square (not just a GCF) must be factored.

sub_skills.name: Exponents and radicals
sub_skills.definition: Rewrite expressions with radicals, rational exponents, negative exponents, or quotients of powers of the same base.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The given expression or choices contain a radical sign, a fractional or negative exponent, or a quotient of powers of the same base, so the answer depends on exponent/radical rules. Products of monomials with only positive integer exponents stay in EE.2.

sub_skills.name: Rational expressions
sub_skills.definition: Add, subtract, simplify or divide fractions whose denominators contain the variable.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: A denominator contains a polynomial with two or more terms, OR two or more fractions with variable denominators must be added/subtracted. Monomial quotients such as h^15q^7/(h^5q^21) are EE.4.

sub_skills.skill_code: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems of Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Rearrange a formula to isolate a variable
sub_skills.definition: Solve a literal equation or formula (two or more letters) for a named variable or expression, possibly through fractions, reciprocals or a square root.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem asks to express a variable or expression 'in terms of' other letters, or to rewrite a formula in a stated form ('Which equation correctly expresses…', 'Which of the following is equivalent to n', 'rewritten in the form v_f = xa + y'). This test wins over NLE.2/NLE.3 even when the formula contains a square root or a variable denominator.

sub_skills.skill_code: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems of Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solve a quadratic or polynomial equation in one variable
sub_skills.definition: Find the solutions (or the sum, product, or a stated form of the solutions) of a one-variable equation whose unknown is squared or appears in a product of linear factors, by square roots, factoring and the zero-product property, completing the square, or the quadratic formula.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: One unknown; the unknown is squared or multiplied by itself (x^2, (x+a)^2, (x-a)(x-b)…), with no absolute value, no radical over the unknown, no unknown in a denominator; and the stem asks for a solution or a quantity built from the solutions, NOT for how many solutions exist (that is NLE.4) and NOT 'in terms of' (NLE.1).

sub_skills.skill_code: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems of Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solve an absolute value, radical, or rational equation in one variable
sub_skills.definition: Solve a one-variable equation in which the unknown sits inside absolute-value bars, under a square root, or in a denominator, including the two-case split, squaring, clearing denominators, and rejecting extraneous or excluded values.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: One unknown and the unknown appears inside absolute-value bars, under a radical sign, or in a denominator; the stem asks for a solution or a quantity built from the solutions. Not 'in terms of' (NLE.1). Also tag NLE.4 if the stem states or asks a solution count.

sub_skills.skill_code: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems of Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Determine the number of real solutions
sub_skills.definition: Decide how many real solutions an equation or system has, or find the constant that forces a stated number of solutions (exactly one / none / more than one), using the discriminant, the sign of a square, or the position of a line relative to a parabola.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem asks 'how many (distinct real) solutions / points of intersection', asks which equation has no real solutions, OR states a solution count as a condition ('has exactly one solution', 'no real solutions', 'intersects … at exactly one point', 'more than one real solution'). Co-tags with NLE.5 when the object is a system.

sub_skills.skill_code: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems of Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solve a system of a linear and a nonlinear equation
sub_skills.definition: Find (or read from a graph) the intersection point(s) of a system in two variables where at least one equation is nonlinear (quadratic, absolute value, radical, xy = k, or f(a) = g(a)), then report x, y, or a combination such as xy or y1 + y2.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives two equations in x and y (or two functions f and g, or a graph of two curves) and at least one is not linear; the question is about their common solution(s)/intersection(s). Co-tags NLE.4 when the stem asks or states the number of solutions.

sub_skills.name: Function notation: evaluate, read and solve input-output
sub_skills.definition: Use a fully or partly specified nonlinear function (equation, graph, or table) to get an output from an input, an input from an output, or an unknown constant from given points.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the asked quantity is a function value, an input value, a y-intercept, an unknown constant found by substituting given points into the function, or a table/graph whose points must match the function; AND the answer choices are not context statements. Exclude when the target is a vertex/extremum, zero found by factoring, growth factor/percent/period, or a transformed rule (those go to NLF.3/4/5; co-tag NLF.1 only if a final f(a) evaluation is still asked).

sub_skills.name: Interpret a nonlinear function in context
sub_skills.definition: State what a point, f(a)=b statement, intercept, vertex, constant/coefficient, or expression means in the real-world situation.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the answer choices (MC) are verbal context statements or context-quantity descriptions (typically 'best interpretation', 'what does X represent', 'which does the model predict', 'best describes'). Choices that are numbers, expressions, equations, or graphs do NOT qualify even if the stem is in context.

sub_skills.name: Exponential growth and decay structure
sub_skills.definition: Write, rewrite, or analyze an exponential function using its growth/decay factor, percent rate, time period in the exponent, or increasing/decreasing behavior.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the function is exponential (a(b)^x, a(b)^(x/k), a^x+b, or described as changing by a constant factor/percent per step) AND the solution needs the base/factor, the percent<->factor conversion, the exponent's time scaling, exponent-rule rewriting of the form, or growth-vs-decay direction. Exponential questions needing only f(0)/f(a) or constants from substituted points are NLF.1 (or NLF.2) only.

sub_skills.name: Quadratic and polynomial structure and models
sub_skills.definition: Use the structure of a quadratic or polynomial (vertex/extremum, axis of symmetry, zeros and factors, multiplicity, standard/vertex/factored forms) or set up and solve a quadratic/polynomial from a verbal or geometric relationship.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the function/equation is a polynomial of degree >= 2 given by equation, table, verbal or geometric description (not a graph to be read directly) AND the question asks for or requires: vertex, min/max, axis of symmetry, zeros/x-intercepts/factors (by factoring, zero product property or symmetry), number of distinct zeros, conversion between forms, OR writing/solving a quadratic/polynomial model from words (area, volume, product of numbers, formula). Reading a vertex/intercept straight off a displayed graph is NLF.1.

sub_skills.name: Transformations of functions
sub_skills.definition: Relate a function to its translation or input-shift: g(x)=f(x)+k, f(x-h), f(x+h), or a shifted graph/table.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem defines one function as a translation/input shift of another (words 'shifted/translated up/down/left/right', or g(x)=f(x±h), y=f(x)±k), or a context change that adds/subtracts a constant to every output (7fe7cf26: platform 2 ft shorter), and the answer depends on applying that shift.

sub_skills.name: Solve a linear equation for its variable
sub_skills.definition: Find the value of the variable that makes a given one-variable linear equation (no real-world context) true, including equations that need distributing, combining like terms, or clearing fractions first.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives a symbolic linear equation with no real-world context AND asks for the value of the variable itself ("what value of x/p/t is the solution", "what is the solution"); not tagged if the requested quantity is any other expression, or if the stem asks how many solutions or for a constant.

sub_skills.name: Find the value of an expression or an equivalent equation without stopping at the variable
sub_skills.definition: Use a given linear equation to get the value of a requested expression in the variable (e.g., 6x - 1, x - 7, 9x, 2 - 4x) or to pick the equation that has the same solution.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives a symbolic linear equation (no context) and EITHER asks for the value of an expression that is not the bare variable ("what is the value of 3x + 8", "x - 5 is between which values") OR asks which equation "has the same solution as" / "is equivalent to" the given one.

sub_skills.name: Translate between a context and a linear equation or expression
sub_skills.definition: Write the linear equation or expression that models a described situation, or interpret what a number or term in a given context equation means.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem describes a situation in words AND the answer choices are equations/expressions in a variable ("which equation represents this situation", "in terms of n") OR the choices are verbal interpretations of a number or term in a given equation ("best interpretation of 2.00x").

sub_skills.name: Solve a context problem for an unknown quantity
sub_skills.definition: Find a numeric quantity in a real-world situation that reduces to one linear equation in one unknown (totals, rates, remaining amounts, perimeters).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem describes a situation in words AND the correct answer is a number (MCQ numeric choices or a grid-in), not an equation, expression, or interpretation.

sub_skills.name: Determine the number of solutions or the constant that sets it
sub_skills.definition: Decide whether a linear equation has zero, one, or infinitely many solutions, or find (or constrain) a constant that makes it have no or infinitely many solutions.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem asks "how many solutions" OR states that the equation has no solution / infinitely many solutions and asks for a constant's value or what must be true.

sub_skills.name: Evaluate or invert a given linear rule
sub_skills.definition: Use a fully specified linear rule (equation, function, or plotted line) to get the output for a given input, or the input that gives a given output.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the answer requires computing f(input) or solving f(x) = output (output not described as an intercept) for a rule whose coefficients are all known numbers or whose graph is shown; also tag when such a computation is the final step after the rule is built (LF.2) or completed (LF.3). Do not tag when the computation is f(0)/f(x)=0 asked as an intercept (LF.5).

sub_skills.name: Build a linear model from a verbal description
sub_skills.definition: Translate a context stated in words (a rate per unit plus a fixed/starting amount, including first-unit-then-additional pricing) into a linear expression or equation.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem gives NO equation for the relationship and states a rate in words ('per', 'each', 'for every', 'additional') and/or a fixed amount that the student must write as an expression (the target may be the equation itself or a value computed from it). Two data points stated in words without a stated rate are LF.3, not LF.2.

sub_skills.name: Determine a linear function from points, a table, values, or slope
sub_skills.definition: Find the slope, the intercept, an unknown constant, or the whole equation of a linear function from two or more (x, y) facts: coordinate pairs, table rows, f(a) = b statements, a stated slope plus a point, or gridline points on a graph.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when at least one of the rule's constants (slope, intercept, or another named constant) is not given as a numeric coefficient and must be obtained from (x, y) information; includes 'which equation defines f' given slope + intercept in words.

sub_skills.name: Interpret slope, intercept, and constants in context
sub_skills.definition: State what a coefficient, constant term, intercept, slope, or function-value statement means in the situation (rate per unit vs. starting value vs. zero-output point), or produce the contextual quantity that is one of them.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem asks for the 'best interpretation'/'meaning'/'what X represents', OR asks for a contextual quantity (per-unit amount, initial amount, change in output for a change in input, fixed dimension) that is answered by identifying the slope or constant of a given model rather than by evaluating it.

sub_skills.name: Intercepts and graph features of a linear function
sub_skills.definition: Find or use the x-intercept, y-intercept, a parallel line's slope, the graph that matches an equation, or a vertical shift y = f(x) + k / sum of functions.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem names an x- or y-intercept, a parallel line, a choice of graphs, or a graph of y = f(x) + k (or h = f + g graphed). Questions that ask for f(0) or an initial amount without naming an intercept are not LF.5.

sub_skills.name: Model a situation with a linear equation
sub_skills.definition: Build the two-variable (or reduced one-variable) equation that a described real-world situation implies.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem is a word context AND either asks which equation represents/models the situation, OR asks for a value while giving no equation, graph or table that relates the quantities (the student must create the relationship).

sub_skills.name: Interpret parts of a contextual linear equation or graph
sub_skills.definition: State what a coefficient, constant, term, variable, ordered pair or difference of coefficients means in context.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem gives a contextual equation or graph and the question asks 'best interpretation' / 'what does N represent' / 'price of each' / 'how many more points per', answerable from structure without solving for an unknown.

sub_skills.name: Find one quantity in context when the other is known
sub_skills.definition: Use a contextual linear relationship to get one variable's value from the other's given value.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Context stem; the value of one variable (or a relation fixing it, e.g. c = 2p, or a point read off a contextual graph) is given and the answer is the value of another quantity in the relationship.

sub_skills.name: Connect a line's equation, graph, table, slope and intercepts
sub_skills.definition: For a single line, move between equation, graph, table, slope, intercepts and points (incl. missing coordinates and unknown constants).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Question asks for a line's slope, intercept, equation, matching table/graph, a missing coordinate, or an unknown constant in its equation, from an equation, graph, table, points or slope; includes contextual graphs/tables when the question asks for the equation.

sub_skills.name: Relate a second line: parallel, perpendicular or translated
sub_skills.definition: Get a second line's slope or equation from a given line via parallel/perpendicular rules or a vertical shift.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem defines one line or graph as parallel to, perpendicular to, or a translation/shift (incl. y = f(x) + k) of another.

sub_skills.skill_code: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solve a system algebraically
sub_skills.definition: Find x, y, or the ordered pair satisfying both equations.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Two equations are given symbolically (or the graphs are said to intersect at (a, b)) and the question asks for x, y, or (x, y).

sub_skills.skill_code: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Value of an expression from a system
sub_skills.definition: Find an expression in the solution (x + y, 39x, x - y, xy, 6(x - 2)) from the system.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The question asks for any quantity other than x alone, y alone, or (x, y).

sub_skills.skill_code: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Number of solutions and conditions on constants
sub_skills.definition: Decide whether a system has zero, one, or infinitely many solutions, find a constant giving a stated count, or describe the solution set of a dependent system.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The question asks how many solutions/intersection points, which system has no solution, which second equation gives no/infinitely many solutions, a constant for no/infinitely many solutions, or which parametric point lies on both coincident lines.

sub_skills.skill_code: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Model a context with a system
sub_skills.definition: Write (and, when asked, solve) a system of two linear equations for a situation with two unknowns and two conditions.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: A situation with two unknown quantities and two stated conditions (totals, 'times as many', 'more than') is given, and the question asks for the system or a value of one unknown.

sub_skills.skill_code: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solutions shown on a graph
sub_skills.definition: Read a system's solution as the intersection of graphed lines, or match a system to its graph.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: A graph of the lines is shown (or the answer choices are graphs) and the question asks for the solution, a matching system, or the number of solutions when a further line is added.

sub_skills.skill_code: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Model a situation with a one-sided inequality or system
sub_skills.definition: Translate a context or verbal statement into a linear inequality (or a system of them) in one or two variables, or interpret a term or point of such a contextual inequality.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem describes a situation in words AND either (a) asks which inequality/system represents it, (b) asks for a value that can only be reached by first writing an inequality that is NOT printed in the stem, or (c) prints a contextual inequality and asks what a term, coefficient or point means. Exclusion: if the only constraint in the stem is a two-sided bound on one quantity (between / minimum and maximum), tag LI.3 instead.

sub_skills.skill_code: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Solve for a boundary value (maximum / minimum)
sub_skills.definition: Isolate the variable in a one-sided linear inequality and turn the result into the extreme value asked for, including whole-number rounding when the context counts objects.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem asks for a maximum, minimum, greatest, least, or 'closest to the maximum possible' value (or a one-sided allowable range whose only other bound is positivity, e.g. 0 < x <= c) AND CB's rationale reaches it by isolating a variable in an inequality. Not tagged when the answer is chosen only by testing membership of given candidates.

sub_skills.skill_code: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Two-sided ranges (compound inequalities)
sub_skills.definition: Write, check membership in, or transform a range a <= x <= b: combine a lower and an upper bound, or push both ends of a range through a multiplication, division or addition.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem states both a lower and an upper bound on the same quantity (between, from X to Y, minimum ... maximum, at least ... no more than, more than ... less than) OR the answer choices are two-sided inequalities whose two bounds both come from the problem (a lower bound that is only positivity, as in 0 < x, does not count).

sub_skills.skill_code: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Test solutions of a given inequality or system
sub_skills.definition: Decide which points, tables of (x, y) pairs, coordinate values or y-ranges satisfy a two-variable inequality or system that is printed symbolically in the stem or choices.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem or choices print an inequality or system in x and y (or in context letters) symbolically AND the question asks which point(s), table, coordinate value, or set of y-values satisfies it, or which system a given point satisfies.

sub_skills.skill_code: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
sub_skills.name: Read an inequality from its graph
sub_skills.definition: Connect a graphed boundary line and shaded half-plane to its inequality, or read solutions directly from the shaded region.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem contains a [FIGURE] of a boundary line with a shaded region (solid or dashed) and the question asks which inequality it represents or which point lies in the solution region.

sub_skills.name: Polygon perimeter and area
sub_skills.definition: Find the perimeter or area of a 2D polygon (rectangle, square, triangle, or a figure built from them), or work back from it to a side length.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the solution computes a perimeter (sum of sides) or area (lw, s², ½bh) of a polygon from numeric lengths, or inverts one to a side length. Do NOT tag when two similar figures are compared and no polygon formula is evaluated with numbers (those are AV.5 only).

sub_skills.name: Circle area and circumference
sub_skills.definition: Use A = πr² or C = 2πr for a circle, including radius/diameter from a given circumference or area.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem gives or asks a plane circle's area, circumference, radius or diameter, OR gives a solid's circular base as a circumference or as an area in π that must be turned back into r. Do NOT tag a cylinder/cone volume where r or d is given and simply substituted into the volume formula.

sub_skills.name: Volume of solids
sub_skills.definition: Compute a volume of a prism, cube, cylinder, cone, sphere/hemisphere (or a stem-given volume formula), or work back from a volume to a dimension.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the solution evaluates or inverts a volume formula (lwh, s³, s²h, Bh, πr²h, ⅓πr²h, ⁴⁄₃πr³, or a formula printed in the stem). A volume that is only given and scaled by k³ without evaluating a formula does not count.

sub_skills.name: Surface area of solids
sub_skills.definition: Find the total or exterior surface area of a prism/cube as the sum of its face areas, or work back from it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the solution adds (or removes) face areas of a solid, or inverts a surface-area expression (6s², 2lw+2lh+2wh). A surface area that is only given and scaled by k² does not count.

sub_skills.name: Similarity and scaling between figures
sub_skills.definition: Carry a stated length factor between two figures to a side, perimeter (×k), area (×k²) or volume (×k³).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem relates corresponding measures of TWO figures multiplicatively ("similar", "k times", "twice the radius", "x% longer/increased", "scale model", "how many times") and the answer requires applying that factor. An additive relation inside one figure ("40 cm longer than the width") does not count.

sub_skills.name: Angle relationships at intersecting and parallel lines
sub_skills.definition: Find or relate angle measures formed where lines cross: vertical angles, angles on a straight line / around a point, and the angle pairs a transversal makes with parallel lines (corresponding, alternate, same-side).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the CB rationale uses at least one of: 'vertical angles', 'linear pair' / 'form a straight line' / 'supplementary' for two adjacent angles on a line, or a transversal pair ('corresponding', 'alternate interior', 'same-side/consecutive interior', 'exterior angles on the same side') across lines stated parallel. Not tagged for the 180 sum of a triangle's interior angles alone (that is LAT.2).

sub_skills.name: Triangle angle sum and exterior angles
sub_skills.definition: Use that a triangle's interior angles sum to 180 degrees (including the right-triangle form: acute angles sum to 90) and the exterior-angle theorem, alone or chained across several triangles.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the CB rationale (or alternate approach used as most direct) invokes 'sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180', 'acute angles of a right triangle are complementary', or 'exterior angle ... equal to the sum of the (remote/nonadjacent) interior angles'.

sub_skills.name: Isosceles and equilateral triangles
sub_skills.definition: Translate equal sides into equal angles (base angles of an isosceles triangle) or into the definition of equilateral, then use the resulting angle or side facts.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem states two sides are equal (e.g., 'AB = AC', 'RT = TU'), states two angles are equal and they must be used as base angles, says 'isosceles' or 'equilateral', or the triangle is shown (by coordinates) to have two equal legs; and the CB rationale uses 'isosceles', 'base angles', or 'all three sides have the same length'. Not tagged when the triangle merely happens to have two equal given angles that are simply summed (fd8745fc).

sub_skills.name: Congruence and similarity: correspondence, criteria, and angle preservation
sub_skills.definition: Use the correspondence between congruent or similar figures (triangles, quadrilaterals, dilations) to transfer angle measures, and decide which information is sufficient to establish similarity or congruence.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the stem says 'congruent', 'similar', or 'dilated' (or asks what is 'sufficient/needed to prove' similarity/congruence) AND the asked quantity is an angle measure, an equal-ratio identity, or a sufficiency choice. If the asked quantity is a side length found from a ratio, tag LAT.5 instead (both when a ratio identity is matched between two right triangles, 933fee1a).

sub_skills.name: Similar figures: proportional side lengths
sub_skills.definition: Find an unknown length (or a length ratio) from similar figures by using a scale factor or a proportion of corresponding sides, including similarity hidden in a figure (shared angle, parallel side, vertical angles, altitude to the hypotenuse) and real-world shadow models.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag when the asked quantity is a length, a ratio of lengths, an area built from such a length, or a possible scale factor, AND the CB rationale writes a proportion of corresponding sides or multiplies by a scale factor ('corresponding sides ... proportional', 'scale factor', 'proportional relationship').

sub_skills.name: Pythagorean theorem: missing side
sub_skills.definition: Find (or write the relation for) a missing side of a right triangle from the other two, including right triangles hidden in rectangles and inscribed figures.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if CB's rationale applies a^2 + b^2 = c^2 (or its rearrangement) to get a length that is not available from a stated special-triangle ratio.

sub_skills.name: Special right triangles (45-45-90, 30-60-90)
sub_skills.definition: Use the fixed side ratios x : x : x*sqrt(2) and x : x*sqrt(3) : 2x (including equilateral-triangle altitudes and radical perimeters).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the rationale names an isosceles right / 45-45-90 or 30-60-90 / special right triangle, or uses 'hypotenuse = sqrt(2) times a leg' or 'side opposite 30 = half the hypotenuse'.

sub_skills.name: Right-triangle trig ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA)
sub_skills.definition: Compute sin/cos/tan of an acute angle from side lengths, or turn a given ratio into side lengths.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the solution writes sin, cos or tan as opposite/adjacent/hypotenuse for a specific acute angle of a right triangle (either direction: sides to ratio or ratio to sides).

sub_skills.name: Trig-ratio relationships: complements and similarity
sub_skills.definition: Use that sin of an angle = cos of its complement, the two acute tangents are reciprocals, and similar triangles share trig ratios / proportional sides.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the rationale uses 'sine ... equal to the cosine of its complement', 'tangents ... reciprocals', 'in similar triangles the [ratio] of corresponding angles are equal', or a similar-triangle side proportion.

sub_skills.name: Circle equation: center and radius
sub_skills.definition: Move between a circle's equation (standard or expanded) and its center/radius: read them, write the equation, complete the square, or apply a translation/radius change.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the solution must read (h,k)/r from an equation or graph, or write/rewrite an equation from (h,k)/r. Not tagged when the point is substituted directly without using the center/radius (b96ff36e).

sub_skills.name: Points and lines relative to a circle in the xy-plane
sub_skills.definition: Use a specific non-center point or a line with a circle in the coordinate plane: on/inside, diameter endpoint, coordinate bounds, tangency to an axis, tangent-line slope.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem names a specific point (other than the center) or a line/axis and the solution uses that point's/line's relation to the circle (lies on, interior, endpoint of a diameter, tangent at it, touches the axis).

sub_skills.name: Arcs, central angles and circumference
sub_skills.definition: Relate arc length/arc measure to the central angle and the whole circle (fraction of circumference, arcs summing to the whole).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem gives or asks for an arc (length or degree measure) or asks for circumference from an arc.

sub_skills.name: Radius-built triangles and tangent segments
sub_skills.definition: Build a triangle from radii and/or tangent segments and use equal radii (isosceles), tangent-perpendicular-to-radius (right angle), or equal tangent segments.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if CB's rationale states 'radii are congruent/equal' to set two triangle sides or base angles, or 'tangent ... perpendicular to the radius', or 'tangent segments ... equal length'.

sub_skills.name: Radian measure and the unit circle
sub_skills.definition: Convert degrees and radians and evaluate sin/cos/tan of radian angles via coterminal angles on the unit circle.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Tag if the stem or a choice expresses an angle in radians (a multiple of pi) or asks for a radian/degree measure, or asks for sin/cos/tan of a radian angle.

sub_skills.skill_code: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
sub_skills.name: Unit conversion (linear units)
sub_skills.definition: Convert a quantity or a rate from one unit to another of the same kind using given or standard conversion factors, single- or multi-step.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Asked quantity is the same physical quantity as a given one but in a different unit, every unit involved is to the first power, AND the student does not have to form a rate between two different kinds of quantity to get it. (Converting the units of a given rate, e.g. yd/h → mi/h, is RAT.1.)

sub_skills.skill_code: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
sub_skills.name: Ratios and proportional scaling
sub_skills.definition: Use a stated ratio (or a quotient/multiple relation between two quantities) to find a missing term, a ratio in simplest form, or how one quantity changes when the other is scaled.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem contains the word 'ratio' (or ':'), OR relates two quantities of the same kind/unitless variables by a quotient or multiple (x/y = 4, t = 4u, 'is 9/10 of'), and the answer comes from that relation.

sub_skills.skill_code: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
sub_skills.name: Rates between different quantities
sub_skills.definition: Compute a rate of one kind of quantity per another (speed, price, output per time) or use one to find an amount, time, or a scaled amount.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem pairs two DIFFERENT kinds of quantity via 'per', 'for every', 'in', 'every' (distance/time, dollars/pounds, items/hour, kg per object) and neither is an area or volume (else RAT.4).

sub_skills.skill_code: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
sub_skills.name: Density and per-area/per-volume rates
sub_skills.definition: Use mass density, population density, pressure, area-per-person, or flux: a rate where one quantity is an area or volume, often computed from a cube or square.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem names density/pressure/flux or a rate whose denominator or factor is a square or cubic unit (people per square mile, square feet per person, grams per cubic cm). Takes priority over RAT.3.

sub_skills.skill_code: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
sub_skills.name: Converting squared or cubed units
sub_skills.definition: Convert a quantity whose unit is raised to a power (square yards ↔ square miles, ft²/h → m²/min, m/s² → mi/min²) using a linear factor raised to that power.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: A unit with an exponent (square, cubic, 'squared') must be converted to another unit. Subsumes RAT.1 for that question (no double tag).

sub_skills.name: Percent of a quantity
sub_skills.definition: Find the part that is a given percent of a given whole (part = p/100 x whole), including percents over 100% stated as 'p% of'.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives a percent and the quantity it is taken OF (words 'p% of', 'of these ... p% are', a tip/share of a total) and the unknown is the resulting amount or expression; the percent is not worded as an increase/decrease ('greater/less than', 'increased/reduced by', 'off', 'tax added').

sub_skills.name: Unknown percent or unknown whole
sub_skills.definition: Given two of part, percent and whole in a 'part is p% of whole' relationship, find the missing percent or the missing whole.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem fixes a 'part is p% of whole' relation (wording 'what percent(age) of', 'is p% of', 'of what number', 'p% of the items ... there are N') and the unknown is the percent p or the whole; no increase/decrease wording attaches to the unknown.

sub_skills.name: Apply or undo a single percent increase or decrease
sub_skills.definition: Turn one percent increase/decrease into the multiplier (1 + p/100) or (1 - p/100) and use it forward (new value), backward (original value), or report the multiplier itself.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem contains an increase/decrease phrase with a GIVEN percent ('p% greater/more/less than', 'increased/reduced/decreased by p%', 'p% off', 'p% tax is added', 'depreciate by p%') and the unknown is the new value, the original value, or the multiplier/expression.

sub_skills.name: Percent change between two values
sub_skills.definition: Find the percent by which one value is greater or less than another: (new - old)/old x 100, or read the percent change off a multiplier.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives (or lets you compute) both the original and the new value, possibly as a multiple like 1.13 x 100 or 0.35x, and the unknown is the percent increase/decrease/change or the p in 'p% greater/less than'.

sub_skills.name: Chained percents (percent of a percent result)
sub_skills.definition: Combine two or more percent relationships whose reference quantities differ, so a later percent is taken of (or compared with) a quantity defined by an earlier one.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem states two or more percents AND they have different bases (the 'of' / 'than' / 'from' quantity of a later percent is the result of, or linked through, an earlier percent: 'of those', 'of the red items', 'each year ... of the previous year's value', 'a is p% of b ... c is q% of a'). Several percents of ONE common whole do not qualify.

sub_skills.skill_code: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
sub_skills.name: Read and interpret a data display
sub_skills.definition: Read counts, categories, or extreme values from a bar graph, frequency table or data table, or build a frequency table from a list.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Answer is a count, a category, a single data value, the min/max, or a sum/difference of read counts (or a frequency table); no mean, median, mode, range or SD has to be computed (a mean printed as a table entry counts as a read value).

sub_skills.skill_code: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
sub_skills.name: Find a measure of center from data
sub_skills.definition: Compute or identify the mean, median or mode of a data set given as a list, table, frequency table, dot plot, histogram or box plot, including a median known only to lie in a bin.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: CB's main rationale computes or reads off the value of a mean, median or mode from the given data values (or bins), including 'which could be the median' and numeric differences between computed centers.

sub_skills.skill_code: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
sub_skills.name: Measures of spread: range and standard deviation
sub_skills.definition: Compute a range, or compare/judge standard deviation or range across data sets or after a change.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem or the keyed choice names range, standard deviation, or 'spread', and the answer depends on that measure.

sub_skills.skill_code: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
sub_skills.name: Use the mean-total relationship
sub_skills.definition: Use mean = total / count to find a missing or removed value, a combined mean, or the mean from a total.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives a mean (or a total and a count, or an equality between means) as a known quantity and asks for an unknown data value, a total, a combined mean, or the mean-sum ratio; the solution multiplies or divides by the count.

sub_skills.skill_code: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
sub_skills.name: Compare measures across data sets or after a change
sub_skills.definition: Decide which measure is greater, equal, or unchanged between two data sets, after adding/removing/changing values, or between mean and median of one set, and which measures a summary determines.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The keyed answer is a relational or 'must/could/can be' statement (greater/less/equal/unchanged/order/which data set/which can be calculated) about measures of center or spread, not a single number.

sub_skills.name: Read data and changes from a graph
sub_skills.definition: Read plotted data values off a scatterplot or line graph and compare them: a single point's value, the highest/lowest point, the change or average rate of change between two plotted points.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem asks about the recorded/actual data (a point's value, greatest/least, change or average rate of change between two given x-values) AND does not ask for a value 'predicted by'/'according to' a line of best fit, model, or trend. A drawn curve that the stem never calls a model counts here.

sub_skills.name: Predict with a fitted model and compare data to it
sub_skills.definition: Use a drawn line/curve of best fit (or the stated trend) to predict y at a given x, or compare actual data points with the model (residual size, points above/below).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem contains 'predicted by', 'according to the line of best fit/model', or 'according to the trend' AND asks for a y-value at a given x, the difference between an actual and predicted value, or a count of points above/below the line. Excludes questions asking for slope/rate per unit (TVD.3).

sub_skills.name: Linear model: direction, slope, intercept, equation, interpretation
sub_skills.definition: Describe a linear trend or line of best fit by its direction, slope and y-intercept: estimate the slope, choose its equation, interpret the slope/rate in context, or transform it when the data are rescaled.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Asks for the association direction, the slope (or 'increase per 1 unit'/'per k units'), an equation of a line of best fit / linear model for a scatterplot, or the meaning of a given linear model's slope; the correct choice/answer is a linear quantity or linear equation.

sub_skills.name: Nonlinear model fitted to a scatterplot
sub_skills.definition: Choose or characterize a quadratic or exponential model (equation or curve) for data shown in a scatterplot.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Data shown in a scatterplot AND the correct answer is a nonlinear model (curve or quadratic/exponential equation) or a parameter of a named exponential/quadratic model of the data.

sub_skills.name: Classify linear vs exponential relationships
sub_skills.definition: Decide whether a relationship given by a description, table, function rule or single graph is linear or exponential and increasing or decreasing, or compare linear with exponential growth.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Choices name a model type (increasing/decreasing linear/exponential), ask which table is (non)linear, or compare a linear and an exponential quantity over time; no scatterplot of data with a fitted model is involved.

sub_skills.name: Probability of an event in the whole group
sub_skills.definition: Probability (or fraction/percent) of one event when the denominator is the entire group: favorable count / total count, no restriction on who is selected.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The asked value is a probability, fraction or percent AND the stem selects from all members ("one of these ...", "a ... from the bag/table") with no "given that", "if the person chosen is/works in ...", "of those/the ... who ...", or "if one of the [subgroup] is selected" restriction.

sub_skills.name: Conditional probability (restricted sample space)
sub_skills.definition: Probability or fraction/percent of an event within a named subgroup: count of (event AND subgroup) / count of subgroup.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem restricts selection to a subgroup with "given that", "if the person chosen [is in X]", "if one of the [X] is selected", "of the/those [X] ...", or "what fraction/percent of [X] ..." AND the correct denominator is that subgroup's total, not the grand total (confirm against the CB rationale's denominator).

sub_skills.name: Find a count from a probability or from totals
sub_skills.definition: Work backward: the probability/fraction (or the grand total) is given and the unknown is a count, a variable in a table, or the category whose count matches a stated fraction.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The asked value is a count or the value of a variable standing for a count (or a category chosen by comparing counts to a given fraction of a total), AND the stem supplies a probability/fraction or a total that the count must satisfy.

sub_skills.name: Complement and exclusion events
sub_skills.definition: The event is defined by exclusion: "not", "neither ... nor", "but does not", or the one remaining category whose count/probability is not given.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem's target event contains "not", "neither", "nor", "but does not", or "other than", OR the target is the only listed category whose count/probability is not given (so it equals the total minus the others). Applied to stem wording, not to whether the table already labels the negated category (see open question).

sub_skills.skill_code: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
sub_skills.name: Estimate a population count from a sample
sub_skills.definition: Scale a random sample's proportion, percent, or mean up to an estimated number (or range of numbers) in the population.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem gives a sample result (count out of n, percent, or mean) and a population size or number of units, and the answer is an estimated COUNT or total for the population (alone or as an interval).

sub_skills.skill_code: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
sub_skills.name: Interpret an estimate with a margin of error
sub_skills.definition: Turn an estimate plus a margin of error into the interval of plausible values for the population parameter and judge statements against it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The stem states an estimate AND a margin of error, and the question asks which conclusion, interpretation, or value is plausible/appropriate.

sub_skills.skill_code: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
sub_skills.name: What the sampling design supports
sub_skills.definition: Judge a conclusion by a property of the sample itself (which population it was drawn from, or its size) rather than by computing an estimate.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The keyed answer is decided by the sampled population or the sample size (e.g. 'only largemouth bass', 'smaller sample size'), and choosing it requires no arithmetic on the estimate. Only 3 CB items exist; see open questions.

sub_skills.skill_code: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
sub_skills.name: Scope of generalization: the largest population the results apply to
sub_skills.definition: Results from a sample selected at random apply to the population it was selected from - no larger group, and more than just the sample.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem says from which group the sample was selected at random, and the choices name groups (or make claims about groups) of different breadth; the key is the sampled population (or the claim restricted to it).

sub_skills.skill_code: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
sub_skills.name: Detect a biased (non-representative) sample
sub_skills.definition: Recognize that a sample not drawn at random from the target population (a subgroup, a convenience location, or self-selected respondents) cannot represent it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: The target population named in the stem differs from the group actually sampled (dog owners only, families at a playground, viewers who chose to answer a web poll), and the key states the sample is biased / not random / not representative.

sub_skills.skill_code: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
sub_skills.name: Sampling variability: a sample result is not a certainty
sub_skills.definition: A random sample's percent does not have to equal the population percent, and another sample need not give the same percent.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Statements claim the population value or another sample's value 'must' equal the observed sample value, and the key is that none of those statements must be true.

sub_skills.name: Restated-meaning blank
sub_skills.definition: Complete a blank whose meaning the text supplies elsewhere as a paraphrase, definition, or set of examples of the same idea.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Fill-in-the-blank stem ("Which choice completes the text..."), AND the word or phrase CB's rationale quotes as the deciding clue is a near-synonym, definition, or examples of the correct answer (typically after a colon/dash, 'that is', 'for example/such as', or in the next sentence). Applies even if a contrast or cause signal is also present, as long as the answer means the same as the quoted clue.

sub_skills.name: Contrasted-meaning blank
sub_skills.definition: Complete a blank whose meaning is the opposite or other side of an idea the text sets against it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Fill-in-the-blank stem, AND a contrast or negation (but, however, although/though, while, whereas, unlike, instead, rather, on the other hand, in contrast, 'challenging the view', not/isn't/hardly/little/unlikely/declines to/fails to) or two juxtaposed facts that differ ('typically X' vs. this case) links the blank to the deciding clue, AND the correct answer means the opposite of that clue (e.g., 'consistent' vs. 'it varies'; 'negligible' vs. 'as many as half').

sub_skills.name: Inferred-relationship blank
sub_skills.definition: Complete a blank whose meaning is not restated or contrasted anywhere but must be inferred from a cause, effect, purpose, or consequence the text states.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Fill-in-the-blank stem, AND no quoted clue is a synonym or opposite of the correct answer, AND the rationale reasons through a cause/result/purpose link (because, since, due to, given, so...that, thus, therefore, in order to, to + verb, so that, by + -ing, as a result, making, allowing) or evidence-to-conclusion step to reach the answer.

sub_skills.name: Given word's meaning in context
sub_skills.definition: Choose the sense of a word or phrase printed in a (literary) passage, usually a common word used in one of its several meanings.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem reads 'As used in the text, what does the word/phrase "X" most nearly mean?' (all 36 such items in this set are from fiction, poetry, drama, or memoir).

sub_skills.name: Main purpose of an informational text
sub_skills.definition: Name the author's overall goal for a whole non-literary text (explain, present a study, argue, describe, challenge a view).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Prompt asks for the 'main purpose' or 'overall purpose' of the text AND the passage does NOT open with 'The following text is (adapted) from ...'.

sub_skills.name: Overall structure of a text
sub_skills.definition: Describe the ordered sequence of moves the whole text makes (e.g., common view then challenge; question then answer; phenomenon, two refuted explanations, plausible third).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Prompt asks for the 'overall structure of the text' (or 'the text's overall structure') and does NOT ask about the function of a specific sentence/portion; applies to literary and informational passages alike.

sub_skills.name: Function of a part in an informational text
sub_skills.definition: Say what logical job an underlined or numbered sentence/portion does relative to the rest of a non-literary text (defines a term, gives an example of a claim, concedes, supplies background, states a limitation, answers a question, poses the problem a study tried to solve).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Prompt contains 'function' (or 'purpose of the underlined portion') about an underlined portion or an Nth sentence AND the passage does NOT open with 'The following text is (adapted) from ...'.

sub_skills.name: Purpose or function in a literary text
sub_skills.definition: In an excerpt from a novel, story, play, poem, or memoir, say what the whole excerpt or a part of it conveys: a character's or speaker's feelings, traits, or relationships, the setting, or what an image stands for.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Passage opens with 'The following text is (adapted) from <author>'s <year> <novel|short story|play|poem|memoir|nonfiction work>' AND the prompt asks for main/overall purpose OR the function of an underlined/numbered part (literary 'overall structure' prompts go to TSP.2 instead).

sub_skills.name: Predict a rebuttal
sub_skills.definition: One author (or a party named in one text) would reject or undercut a specific claim, conclusion, or view in the other text, conceding none of it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem asks how a party in one text would respond to / characterize / say about something in the other text, AND (a) CB's rationale or the correct choice uses rejection language (disagree, challenge, dispute, counter, contradict, questionable, misconception, illogical, not supported) OR (b) the correct choice asserts the target is wrong or offers a competing claim, with NO concession clause and NO scope limiter from the CTC.2 list. Rejection language overrides a limiter (e.g. d6c77ae5 'questionable ... incomplete' -> CTC.1).

sub_skills.name: Predict a qualified (yes-but) response
sub_skills.definition: One author would partly accept the other text's claim but limit, complicate, or temper it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Response stem (as CTC.1) AND the correct choice or CB rationale contains a concession (agree, concede, acknowledge, understandable, while/although X, even though) OR the correct choice contains a scope limiter from this closed list: 'not the only', 'not exclusively', 'not only', 'incomplete', 'overly', 'not inevitably', 'overlooks/fails to consider certain aspects', 'instead of completely' -- AND CB's rationale does not use the CTC.1 rejection verbs. 'not necessarily' is NOT on the list (see open questions).

sub_skills.name: Predict a supportive or applied response
sub_skills.definition: One text's position is used to explain, solve, confirm, extend, or apply to the claim, problem, finding, or situation in the other text.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Response stem (as CTC.1) AND the correct choice accepts the target without disagreement or limiter and states that the responder's idea solves it, prevents it, supports it, makes it expected/unsurprising, contributes to its goal, or applies its advice to a described situation.

sub_skills.name: Identify common ground
sub_skills.definition: Find the statement both texts (or the named parties in each) would accept, usually beneath their disagreement.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem contains 'both ... would most likely agree' or 'X (Text 1) and Y (Text 2) would most likely agree'.

sub_skills.name: Describe the difference or relationship between the texts
sub_skills.definition: State how the two authors' views differ, or how Text 2 functions relative to Text 1.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem contains 'best describes a difference in how' or 'best describes how Text 1 and Text 2 relate'.

sub_skills.name: Compare or contrast two or more items
sub_skills.definition: Write a sentence that relates two (or more) named items: a similarity, a difference, a comparison of amounts, or the order of two events.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Goal sentence names two or more items AND contains one of: similarity, difference/differ(s), contrast, compare, 'order in which', relative, highest, 'different orders'.

sub_skills.name: Fit the sentence to a stated audience
sub_skills.definition: Introduce, describe, or present something to an audience the goal labels as already familiar, unfamiliar, or new: add background for an unfamiliar or new audience, leave it out for a familiar one.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Goal sentence contains the word 'audience' (e.g. 'to an audience unfamiliar with', 'already familiar with', 'to a new audience').

sub_skills.name: Report a research study
sub_skills.definition: Present or emphasize a study as a whole or one of its parts (aim, method, findings, results, conclusion, or the sequence the researchers proposed).
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Goal sentence contains study (not 'field of study'), research, researchers, findings, results, conclusion, methodology, or aim, AND does not ask for a generalization.

sub_skills.name: Generalize, define, or give an example
sub_skills.definition: Make (and support) a generalization about a category, define a term or explain what something is, or give or illustrate an example.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Goal sentence contains generalization, define, example, illustrate, or 'explain what a ...'.

sub_skills.name: Focus on one named feature of one subject
sub_skills.definition: Write a sentence about a single subject that delivers the one feature the goal names: a fact (where, when, how many, name), a cause, advantage, significance or origin, a description or overview, a quotation-based claim, or a narrative opening.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: None of the RS.1 to RS.4 tests fire (residual sub-skill). The goal names one subject plus the feature to deliver.

sub_skills.name: Contrast and concession
sub_skills.definition: The sentence after the blank goes against, qualifies, is an exception to, or is an alternative to the idea before it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Keyed transition is in the TRN.1 lexicon (however, by/in contrast, conversely, on the other hand, in/by comparison (differing items), nevertheless, nonetheless, still, though, that said, granted, of course, instead, alternatively, on the contrary), and CB rationale for the key uses contrasts / despite / exception / qualification / alternative / disagreement / acknowledges a limitation.

sub_skills.name: Cause, result and purpose
sub_skills.definition: The sentence after the blank is a result, consequence, logical conclusion, or goal-driven action that follows from the idea before it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Keyed transition is in the TRN.2 lexicon (as a result, therefore, thus, hence, consequently, for this reason, accordingly, as such, in turn, with this in mind, to that end, in so doing, fittingly; also "then" when CB says the claim "follows logically" (42e6cc83)), and CB rationale for the key uses result / consequence / follows logically / product of a goal / in accordance with / fitting outcome.

sub_skills.name: Addition and similarity
sub_skills.definition: The sentence after the blank adds a separate new point, or a parallel point that is like the one before it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Keyed transition is in the TRN.3 lexicon (in addition, additionally, moreover, furthermore, what’s more, similarly, likewise; also "second" when CB calls it a second supporting point (82ec9628)), and CB rationale for the key uses additional / separate / adds new information / similar / second supporting point.

sub_skills.name: Example, specification, restatement and emphasis
sub_skills.definition: The sentence after the blank develops the SAME point: gives an example of it, specifies its details, restates or clarifies it, or emphasizes it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Keyed transition is in the TRN.4 lexicon (for example, for instance, specifically, in particular, to be exact, that is, in other words, in fact, indeed, in many cases, more often), and CB rationale for the key uses example / exemplifies / specific, precise details / restatement / clarifies / emphasizes and supports / elaborates on the same idea.

sub_skills.name: Time, sequence and place
sub_skills.definition: The sentence after the blank is placed relative to the idea before it in time (before, after, at the same time, now, in the end), as a step in a process or list, or in a place.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Keyed transition is in the TRN.5 lexicon (next, then, later, earlier, previously, afterward, finally, eventually, ultimately, today, currently, meanwhile, increasingly, again and again, first, second (step in a process), there), and CB rationale for the key uses next step / chronological sequence / occurred after or before / simultaneous / present day / conclusion of a process / multiple times / location.

sub_skills.name: Identify the central idea of the whole text
sub_skills.definition: Determine the single claim, topic, purpose or question that the whole text develops, as opposed to any one detail in it.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem asks for the text's main idea, main topic, main purpose, main idea about a named subject, 'what is happening in the text', or 'which question does the text most directly attempt to answer'. Tag on stem wording alone.

sub_skills.name: Retrieve an explicitly stated key detail
sub_skills.definition: Find a fact, reason, method, result, difference or view that the text states outright and recognize it in reworded form.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem is 'According to the text...', 'What does the text say/indicate...', 'The text makes which point...', 'In the text, which point does X most directly make', or 'as presented in the text', AND the stem contains none of the CID.3 markers. Single listed exception: 11a9f635 ('indicate' stem, CB rationale says 'implies') goes to CID.3. Note 'what do some historians suggest' (9fe7aafa) is CID.2: 'suggest' there is the historians' verb, not the text's.

sub_skills.name: Draw a conclusion the details support but do not state
sub_skills.definition: Combine or extend stated details to reach a conclusion, likely consequence, or position the text supports without saying it in one sentence.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem asks what the text '(most strongly) suggests', what is 'most likely', which statement is 'best/most strongly supported', what 'can be concluded' or 'inferred', what someone 'would most likely agree with', or begins 'Based on the text'; plus 11a9f635. Not tagged if the stem is a CID.1 stem.

sub_skills.name: Characterize a person's feelings, traits or attitudes in a literary text
sub_skills.definition: Name a character's, narrator's or speaker's feeling, trait, motive, or attitude toward / regard for someone, from description and action. Co-tagged with CID.1/2/3.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Passage is introduced as from a novel, short story, poem, play or memoir AND the correct choice's content is a feeling, personality trait, motive, or attitude/regard (e.g. 'annoyed', 'delighted', 'remarkably mature', 'holds Thornton in higher regard', 'few feel concerned he will divulge'). sub_skills.name: Read data accurately from a table or graph

sub_skills.name: Use data as evidence for a claim
sub_skills.definition: Select data from a table or graph that support, weaken, illustrate, or complete a claim, conclusion, hypothesis, or example stated in the text, where accurate data can still fail to bear on the claim.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem refers to data in a table/graph AND at least one incorrect choice is rejected by CB because it does not support/weaken/illustrate/complete the claim (e.g., 'although it accurately describes the graph...', 'isn't relevant', 'doesn't include the ... for comparison', or conflicts with the text's stated reasoning) rather than only because it misreads the data.

sub_skills.name: Choose a finding or source statement that supports or weakens a claim
sub_skills.definition: Select a hypothetical finding/statement/detail, or a quotation from a non-literary source (historian, critic, article, participant, survey respondent, interviewee), that would most directly support, illustrate, weaken, or challenge a claim, hypothesis, conclusion, or explanation in an informational text.
sub_skills.inclusion_test: No table/graph is needed AND the stem asks for a 'finding', 'statement', 'detail', 'response', or 'quotation from a/an [person or source about the subject]' (often 'if true') that would support/illustrate/weaken/undermine/challenge a claim; choices are descriptions of results or facts, or quotations by people other than the author of the work named in the text.

sub_skills.name: Choose a quotation from a named work that illustrates a claim about it

sub_skills.inclusion_test: Stem reads 'Which quotation from [title of the work named in the text]' (including 'a translation of [title]', 'the poem', '[character]'s letters') or 'uses a quotation from [title] to illustrate the claim', AND all choices are excerpts from that work.

sub_skills.name: Draw a conclusion from a comparison

sub_skills.name: Chain stated premises to a consequence

sub_skills.inclusion_test: Default class: the correct choice follows by joining two or more stated premises (or applying a stated rule/theory/definition to a stated case) and none of INF.5, INF.3, INF.4, INF.1 applies. sub_skills.name: Generalize from specific cases
